What changes when a State view paints blocks

Left: the state as the national map already draws it, districts filled from district values. Right: the same state filled from block values. Same ruler, same ramp. Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Goa. Source docs\diagnostics\heat_risk_pilot\cdf_support.csv.

Rescaling is on. Each panel now stretches its own observed range across the full ramp, so identical colours no longer mean identical scores — not between the two panels, not between states, and not between one selection and the next. Watch Goa: a two-point spread painted from blue to red.

The bracket on each colourbar marks the range actually present in that panel. Under the frozen domain it is the honest way to show a state that genuinely occupies a narrow slice of the national scale — the fill stays comparable and the reader still sees the spread.
